main_text.p: Externus calor Elementaris est igneus, qui efficit duplices halitus, Ἀτμὶς.'Ἀτμίδα[?] seu vaporem & Θυμίασιν.

Ἀτμὶς.'Ἀτμὶς est halitus quidam calidus, tenuis, (ideoq; levis & furfum tendens) & humidus, humectans ea quæ attingit. Hic educitur ab igni urgente, ex corporibus humidis tantum ἀκαυστοις[?], quæ nihil ficci terrei, aut perparum habent, aut in quibꝰ simul humor aut terreum dominatur.

p.i: Sic aqua ab igne urgente in halitus resolvitur: terra etiam madefacta, & lutum humidum, humorem solum resolutum in vaporem exhalant, terreo remanente.

main_text.p: Θυμίασις.Θυμίασις est halitus calidus & siccus, a terreis potissimum partibus, humore aliquo præditis cremabili attenuatus, qui propter siccitatem non humectat, sed calore tantum inficit id, quod attingit.
Eius genera sex.Hujus halitus genera Sex numerantur.
1. Θυμίαμα.Primum dicitur Θυμίαμα, estq; odora quædam θυμίασις, eorum scilicet, quæ suffitibus idonea sunt.

page.notes: Margin Greek labels read as Ἀτμὶς, Θυμίασις, and 1. Θυμίαμα; the exact accents are doubtful. The Greek word after "seu vaporem &" is uncertain (ἀτμίδα?, θυμίασιν). The Greek word ἀκαυστοις is uncertain and marked [?]. The first line of the page may continue a sentence from the previous page, but it is printed as an indented opening, so no cont attribute is set. "quib9" is read as quibꝰ.
